output.methodChoice: Collected X3 (shipping instructions and product-master change history) and X6 (controller downloads). Compared temperature setpoints, transit days, fungicide use and decay across K1–K9.
output.brief: The rejections were most likely caused by a wrong temperature setting, not the fungicide, the carrier's equipment, or the growers. When the Tallis system was introduced on 3-4 August, it filled the Meridane carriage temperature from a product record copied from an avocado template, so the Meridane mandarin containers were instructed to 7°C instead of the 4°C specification. The carrier's units ran at 7°C as instructed. The five rejected containers were exactly the 7°C Meridane ones; the 4°C containers, including Pellacor-treated ones, passed. Confidence is fairly high. Next: correct PRD-MAND-01 to 4°C now, and have Meridane reset the container at sea and the one queued for 10 October. Add a check that compares reefer settings with the product specification. Do not pursue the refrigeration claim against Meridane, suspend Lower Serra growers, or claim against Brindle yet. The fungicide change is unlikely to be the cause, though Lower Serra fruit may add some risk, which can be tested later.
